one_liner: Cryptocurrency exchange offering spot, futures, and wallet trading via REST and WebSocket APIs.

auth.evidence_quote: Use the secretKey of your API key as the signing key for the HMAC-SHA-256 algorithm.
auth.notes: SIGNED endpoints require api key plus HMAC (or RSA/Ed25519) signature; no OAuth2 for third-party account access, so a third party would need each user's own API key/secret.

access.evidence_quote: Both API key and secret key are sensitive. Never share them with anyone.
access.notes: Any registered Binance user can generate API keys for free; no separate developer program gate found, though KYC on the underlying account is implied.

api.evidence_quote: The last 4 endpoints in the point above (api1-api4) should give better performance but have less stability.
api.notes: Binance also offers WebSocket streams (used 'webhook_only' loosely is inaccurate; real-time is via WebSocket not webhooks — noting protocols may need correction to exclude webhook_only in pass 2). Endpoint count not confirmed but spot+futures+margin APIs are extensive (broad).

verdict.rationale: Free self-serve API key generation with HMAC-signed REST API makes basic building possible immediately, though per-user keys are needed for account-specific actions.
